findings.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so a waiting caller can redundantly reload and overwrite a successful cache entry with a later failure.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — The write-lock path never rechecks the cache, so callers that concurrently observe a cold cache serialize redundant full manifest reads and make startup latency and I/O scale with the number of racing requests.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No concurrent cold-cache test catches the missing post-lock cache recheck, so simultaneous production callers reload the manifest serially instead of sharing the first result.

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — The write-lock path never rechecks the cache, so callers that concurrently observe a cold cache serialize redundant full manifest reads and make startup latency and I/O scale with the number of racing requests.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that after acquiring the write lock at line 48, the code doesn't recheck if another goroutine already populated the cache while waiting for the lock. This is a classic double-checked locking pattern issue. While not a correctness bug (the code will still work correctly), it's a valid performance concern - multiple concurrent requests hitting a cold cache will all serialize and redundantly read the manifest. This is a real, specific, diff-grounded issue about the implementation pattern chosen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No concurrent cold-cache test catches the missing post-lock cache recheck, so simultaneous production callers reload the manifest serially instead of sharing the first result.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the diff. After acquiring the write lock at line 48, the code doesn't recheck if entryPointAssetsCache is still nil before proceeding to reload the manifest. This is a classic double-checked locking bug - multiple goroutines could pass the initial RLock check (when cache is nil), then each would sequentially acquire the write lock and reload the manifest, instead of the second+ goroutines finding the cache already populated by the first. The fix should include a second check after acquiring the write lock: 'if entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }'
